title: 人体の構造と機能
subtitle: Structure and Function in Physiology
educationalGoal: Human Structure and Function majors can explain how the human body works, based on a deep understanding of the relationship between physiology and anatomy. This is the first course designed to provide foundational knowledge of the human body deemed necessary for discipline-specific courses in neuroscience and brain science. This course introduces not only the proximal factors, but also the ultimate factors of the mechanisms of the human body.
advice: This course will provide information that should enable the student to explain: 1. Generic skills and science literacy (logical thinking, critical thinking, knowledge synthesis). 2. Difference between science and religion (originality, falsifiability, plagiarism). 3. Difference between life and stone (purpose of life, purposiveness, ultimate factor). 4. Evolution of life (mutation, fitness, natural selection, selective pressure, polymorphism). 5. Chemical context of life (organic compounds: carbohydrates, fats, proteins and nucleic acids, etc.). 6. Cell structure and function (cell membrane, organelles, movement across membranes, diffusion, osmosis, active transport). 7. Metabolic pathway (catabolic pathway and anabolic pathway, enzyme, cellular respiration, fermentation) 8. Protein structure and function. 9. Synthesis of protein (DNA to RNA: transcription, translation: making protein from RNA template). 10. Intercellular signaling (ion channel, receptor, transporter). 11. Regulation of blood sugar and the mechanism of diabetes. 12. Endocrine system (hormones and target receptors, feedback regulation). 13. Nervous system (neurons, synapses, resting potential, action potential, neurotransmitters). 14. Significance of homeostasis at the cellular, tissue, organ, and organismal levels.
requiredKnowledge: General knowledge of chemistry, physics, and math is required. In order to understand the information presented, the habit of studying the background information is required.

activityGoals.body: Explain human structure and function from an evolutionary perspective.
Explain the structure and function of the human body, its organs, and tissues.
Explain regulation of blood sugar and the mechanism of diabetes.
Explain human functions through signaling at the intracellular and intercellular levels.
